sentences.text: Throughout this week, Russia has accused Nato of preparing to blockade its territory, which borders Lithuania and Poland, warning that it would even be prepared to use nuclear weapons if the West tried to cut off Kaliningrad from the rest of Russia.

sentences.text: Nato has sought to calm the situation, stressing that it was a defensive alliance and urging Moscow to stop its "nuclear threats".

sentences.text: It's been a difficult few years for Nike.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: The largest sportswear brand on the planet, named after the ancient Greek goddess of victory, has been losing of late.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: Losing sales, losing customers and losing ground to its rivals.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: The one-time industry disruptor is now the establishment and in the middle of a tricky turnaround plan aimed at clinging on to market dominance.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: Nike's latest financial results show signs a turnaround strategy put in place by company veteran Elliott Hill, who was coaxed out of retirement two years ago to lead the firm, is working - but the pace of change is more marathon than sprint.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: However, its recovery has been dented by the loss of football star Kylian Mbappé, who ended his 20-year association with the brand last week to join fast-growing Swiss rival, On.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: The Real Madrid striker's departure raises the question of whether Nike can remain the top logo for not just elite athletes, but also the fans that idolise them.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: To be clear, Nike is still a mega brand and popular the world over.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: But missteps have seen hundreds of billions of dollars wiped off its stock market value as its share price tumbled by 75% over five years.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: Last month, Nike was ejected from the S&P 100 stock market index of the biggest blue-chip firms in the US.

sentences.text: And can Hill turn things around?
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: Matt Powell, a veteran analyst and adviser in the sports retail industry, reckons Nike has made "several strategic errors" which have been difficult to reverse, including cutting ties with retailers to sell only direct to customers online and making limited editions items more available.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: "The more broadly available those shoes became, the fewer people were interested," Powell says.
sentences.article_title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo

sentences.text: Other self-inflicted wounds he suggests include spending research and development cash on digital operations rather than new products.

sentences.text: "They really shut down their innovation on product.

sentences.text: The meeting came as some tech executives and experts have called for tighter oversight of AI, citing concerns about the potential risks it poses to humanity.

sentences.text: Here are three key takeaways from Trump's tech summit at the White House.

sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: Under the agreement, which Trump posted online , external , the companies are responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: The firms also agreed to implement safeguards to keep models operating as intended and quickly detect and fix any issues.
sentences.article_title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit

sentences.text: "It's almost like a constitution, in a way," Trump said.

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The final instalment of Alan Milburn's review into Neets is due to be published this autumn He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn also emphasised the difficulty some young people face when trying to find work experience placements.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "There are about four in ten people aged 14-16 who aren't getting any work experience at all," he said.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Education is devolved in the UK, so while Milburn's review looks at the picture in all four nations, his recommendations regarding education are specific to England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Currently in England, careers guidance must be offered to students aged 11-18 and work experience is not statutory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The government has said its vision , external is to "guarantee two weeks' worth of work experience for every young person" in England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: In both Scotland and Wales, career-based learning is already a requirement in schools for students as young as three.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Just let them be little kids.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids." But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "I think it's a good idea," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of school leaders' union National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT), warns of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Whenever new mandatory requirements are proposed, it is important to be clear about what might have to give way to make room for them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Whiteman also highlights the value of existing programmes such as "Primary Futures", which bring in volunteers from different professions into schools to "challenge stereotypes and raise aspirations".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "The earlier young people can begin to make connections between what they learn in school and the possibilities that lie ahead, the better," Whiteman says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The BBC licence fee should be extended to cover services other than TV and the corporation's charter review should be scrapped and made permanent, an influential group of MPs has said.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: The report from the House of Commons' cross-party culture and media committee comes ahead of the government finalising its proposals for the next BBC royal charter later this year, which will set out how the broadcaster is funded, regulated and governed from 2028.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: In its recommendations, the DCMS committee also said that political appointments to the BBC board should end, to improve public trust.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: The report also said the next charter should be made permanent, so that the BBC's funding and existence is not called into question every 10 years.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: They said the current renewal process "creates an avoidable opportunity for political interference which has damaged the perception of the BBC's independence".
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: "It also creates a disproportionate distraction for the BBC when it needs to be focused on its mission to inform, educate and entertain.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: We therefore recommend the next BBC charter be a permanent charter and not include an end date." When making recommendations about the licence fee, the DCMS said its current model was "outdated and no longer fit for purpose", and also suggested that the BBC reduced the cost from its current price of £180 per year.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: Schitt's Creek was snapped up by the BBC after the comedy series left Netflix The committee also said the BBC should not pay "over the odds" for the rights to overseas hits such as Suits and Schitt's Creek.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: Although the BBC produces a lot of its own programmes, the corporation buys some international shows for its TV channels and iPlayer streaming platform.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: The MPs' report said the BBC could "spend more wisely when competing for programming".
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: Overall, the BBC brings "immeasurable benefits" to society but needs reform of the TV licence fee to avoid a fate of "managed decline", they said.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: Committee chair Dame Caroline Dinenage said the report , external comes at "a pivotal moment for the BBC", which is grappling with changing media habits, declining income and negotiations with the government over how it is paid for.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: Dame Caroline said the government "must ensure the BBC has a universal and sustainable source of funding".
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: But, she added, the BBC "can play its part by sweating its assets and boxing clever for the licence payer by ending illogical practices such as outbidding commercial rivals for overseas hits such as Suits, Schitt's Creek and Scooby Doo".
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: The rights to air all three programmes were bought by the BBC after contracts with other networks or streaming services expired.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: "At a time of constrained resources, the BBC should not be paying over the odds for overseas content, particularly when it's a bidding war against commercial UK broadcasters," the committee said.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: The MPs added that they "did not believe that this provides value for money for the licence fee payer".
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: The BBC argued that it spends less than 5% of its content budget on acquiring shows, less than other broadcasters, and they are a cost-effective way of delivering high-quality content to audiences who go on to discover homegrown programming.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: Suits, starring the future Duchess of Sussex (second right, in 2012), has attracted new audiences in recent years Dame Caroline said: "For all its faults, the BBC drives our creative economy, supports our democracy through media sovereignty, and delivers world-class entertainment and moments that bring us together.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: "Like a much-loved family member, we may criticise and grumble about the BBC but we would miss it enormously if it were no longer here for us." The committee said there were "considerable challenges" for the BBC and warned that the current TV licence fee is "outdated and no longer fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: Currently, about 94% of individuals use the BBC each month but only 80% of households pay for a TV licence, the MPs noted.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: "The licence fee should be reformed so it is no longer linked to the consumption of live TV or to a particular device, such as a television set," the committee said.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: Earlier this week, Channel 4 chief executive Priya Dogra said , external she was open to her network's content being hosted on iPlayer.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: The report also called for the end of political appointments to the BBC board, to improve governance and remain trusted by the public.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: And the committee recommended that the BBC is given new public purposes relating to innovation and technology and combating misinformation and disinformation.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: The BBC welcomed the report, which it said made "some important and interesting recommendations on the future of the BBC".
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: A BBC spokesperson said: "We have consistently argued that the current funding model is outdated and needs reform, so we welcome the Committee's support for maintaining universal funding while overhauling the licence fee.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: "We are also pleased to see their recognition of the vital work of the World Service, with a clear recommendation that responsibility for funding should return fully to Government.
sentences.article_title: MPs recommend BBC charter renewal is scrapped and licence fee is extended beyond TV

sentences.text: "At a time of huge disruption in the media, the BBC's trust, reach and creative strength remain unparalleled.

sentences.text: Tory leader Kemi Badenoch (left) with shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately in London last week The Conservatives have said they would introduce new work requirements for under-25s claiming benefits in a "tough love" approach to youth joblessness.

sentences.article_title: Doctors say radical plan to merge Scotland's health boards should be scrapped

sentences.article_title: Doctors say radical plan to merge Scotland's health boards should be scrapped

sentences.article_title: Doctors say radical plan to merge Scotland's health boards should be scrapped

sentences.text: The GP from Wester Hailes in Edinburgh, who took up the role with BMA Scotland just a few weeks ago, stressed that doctors did not deny that the NHS needed to change.

sentences.article_title: Doctors say radical plan to merge Scotland's health boards should be scrapped

sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But planning a harvest is tricky.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Thames Water has apologised to a customer after trying to take £145,000 from his bank account due to a meter reading error by the company.

sentences.text: The Governor of the Bank of England has said regulating artificial intelligence (AI)  "is not the right place to start" but instead called first for "rigorous" testing to find vulnerabilities and create safeguards to contain risk.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: Writing his first-ever article for Substack, Andrew Bailey said the risks around AI were "real and increasingly significant".
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: He said AI development should not be halted or prohibited - "on the contrary, the benefits are immense" - but added there must be a system for intervention and to establish boundaries in which AI operates.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: The debate about the potential risks surrounding the rapid development of AI and what it means for humanity has intensified in recent weeks.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: The bosses of leading AI firms such as Anthropic and OpenAI have called for development of the technology to slow down and for an internationally co-ordinated approach assessing risks and putting safeguards in place.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: OpenAI recently announced that it would not release its latest AI model due to safety concerns .
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons OpenAI scraps rollout of new model over safety concerns Under the agreement, the companies are responsible for ensuring the safety of their own technology.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: In the UK, Bailey said "important work" was underway in testing AI - the UK has set up the AI Security Institute - which, he said, should help form part of a set of standards.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: "But the pace of progress must accelerate," the bank governor said, though he added: "We should proceed with a degree of humility." He said, with testing, there will be failures and "models will behave unexpectedly".
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: But, he said: "That is not evidence that testing has failed, rather it is evidence of why testing is necessary." Bailey said that testing should not be seen as an alternative to future regulation - over time a more formal regulatory framework might emerge.
sentences.article_title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey

sentences.text: "But regulation is not, in my view, the right place to start." Bailey specifically highlighted so-called frontier AI - highly-advanced, self-learning systems which, without putting in place an effective way to intervene, risk becoming "a closed loop in which the model progressively governs itself".

sentences.text: Emerald Battery Labs founders (left to right) Aric Stocks, Kjell Schroder, David Bell "We think sodium ion […] is going to make up 80% of the market," says David Bell, co-founder and chief executive of Seattle-based Emerald Battery Labs.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Bell declined to share details of the battery design his firm is working on, though he says Emerald too is currently relying on China-sourced sodium ion cells as they develop their initial product: 12 volt auxiliary batteries for vehicles, currently supplied to unnamed commercial fleets in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We took a look at the market and said 'Hey, no-one's trying to attack this space, let's have Emerald Battery Labs attack it'," says Bell.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The firm's next goal is to develop new anodes for US-produced sodium ion cells.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Another company, Peak Energy, based in California and Colorado, announced a partnership with General Motors (GM) in June.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The pair aim to develop a US supply chain for sodium ion batteries, in order to enable large-scale energy storage for electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Peak Energy is also, at present, relying on China-sourced cells for its first installations, but hopes to help GM launch a US-based production facility in Michigan "by the end of 2028", says Cameron Dales, president and co-founder.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "China does not have an insurmountable lead in sodium ion batteries," he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Alysm sodium ion batteries are made in the US One reason US companies feel they can compete is because of the electricity demand boom from data centres, which are contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Data centre-driven demand is also rising in other places around the world, including the UK .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is an "opportunity" says Drew Buckley, chief executive at ESS Tech, headquartered in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: He points out that sodium ion batteries could help distribute renewable energy to data centres.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And those batteries should be cheaper to run than lithium ion alternatives, since they are not expected to require as much cooling.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: ESS Tech is working with Alsym, another US firm that is planning to ship "hundreds" of megawatt hours' worth of sodium ion batteries – made in the US – by 2027.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Hasa says that it will be "challenging" for companies to establish mass production of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And she also notes that, while this type of battery is often touted as much safer than lithium ion, they do not come with zero fire risk.

sentences.text: But if any firms can succeed in this space, they could enable new strategic choices, she adds – helping to avoid wastage of renewable electricity and potentially keeping energy costs low.

sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The only noise is the gentle clang of the bells around the animals' necks.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This would be an idyllic scene were it not for the blackened pine and oak trees all around, the legacy of a devastating recent wildfire.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was immense, I've never seen anything like it," says Izquierdo, whose family have been farming here for 200 years.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The fire, in late July, merged with two others, burning a total of around 80,000 hectares (200,000 acres), making it the biggest blaze Spain has ever registered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: It consumed more than two-thirds of Izquierdo's land and killed 12 of his 85 cows.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another eight animals had to be put down because of their injuries.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: All the hay he had gathered to feed his cows in the winter was also burned.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "For us farmers, the summers are becoming more and more worrying, because they are getting hotter," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It rains less, the wet season ends earlier and the autumn starts much later." For farmers, such conditions are synonymous with fires.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "If you don't think about the wildfires too much, you feel okay," Izquierdo says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "But when a fire starts in a nearby village you start wondering – 'and what if we're next?'." Wildfires are one of several symptoms of climate change which in recent years have had a substantial impact on Spain's economy, as well as contributing to shocking human tragedies.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: World Weather Attribution, an international research organisation, found that the extreme conditions that drove record-breaking fires in Spain and Portugal in 2025 were 40 times more likely , external to happen due to the warming climate.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The ultimate reason for the greater frequency and intensity of these kinds of fires has to be attributed to the increase in greenhouse gases caused mainly by the generalised use of fossil fuels," said Ernesto Rodríguez Camino, president of the Spanish Meteorology Association.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Socialist Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has described the fires in dramatic terms, placing Spain in the front line of an environmental crisis.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The climate emergency kills," he said in July, during a visit to the southern province of Almería where a wildfire claimed 15 lives.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Research found that extreme heat and resulting fires in Spain were now 40 times more likely This year, around 300,000 hectares of land have been burned in Spain, according to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), approximately half the total affected in the entire European Union.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The local authorities in Castilla y León, the region most heavily affected by this year's massive fire near Madrid, are offering compensation – between €5,500 ($6,300; £4,700) and €25,000 ($29,000; £21,000) to each farmer – depending on the damage suffered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: But Izquierdo estimates that this will cover less than half of his losses.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: For decades, Spain's warm climate has been a boon for one of its other biggest industries - tourism.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Sun-drenched resorts along the Mediterranean coast, and in the Balearic and Canary Islands, have driven the country's growth as a tourist hub.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This year, close to 100 million foreigners are expected to come to Spain, making it the second most-visited country in the world, just behind France.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are signs that the heat is becoming too much for some travellers.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, this summer tested their tolerance of heat, with the country registering a record-breaking 61 days of heatwaves that continued into early September.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Toledo repeatedly saw temperatures in excess of 40C.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It's quite difficult to do the tours in the summer," says guide Diego Esteban, of the company Visit Toledo.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We need to adapt, whether it is those of us who work in the tourism industry or the locals." When leading tours in the summer months, Esteban makes sure that there are frequent stops, drinking water is provided and that the itineraries include plenty of shade.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he would like to see more shade and drinking fountains available.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He says the heat has started to change the timing of the tourist season, bringing many more visitors during the cooler months of spring and autumn.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Warmer summers have also encouraged the so-called "coolcation" trend, whereby Spanish travellers seek out cooler areas to spend their holidays, typically in the north of the country.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another consequence of Spain's warming climate has been drought.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: In 2024, after three years of minimal rainfall, the north-eastern region of Catalonia temporarily introduced stringent restrictions on water use, including a 25% reduction for industry and an 80% reduction for crop farming.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Heavy rainfall since then has lifted the restrictions, but the drought had a major impact on the local economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The most dramatic and tragic natural phenomenon Spain has seen in recent years were flash floods that killed 237 people in the east of the country in October 2024, centred on the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spanish meteorological research group Climatoc-Lab described it as "a manifestation of how global warming alters the hydrological cycle".
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Valencia Chamber of Commerce estimated that the floods caused €4.5bn in direct damage.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Thousands of businesses were affected, some literally washed away by the floodwater, while others were able to resume operations after a lengthy recovery.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was a disaster, both in terms of the lives lost and the impact on businesses, on workers, employers and ordinary people," says Laura Llácer Álvarez, manager of the Fepeval federation of industrial parks in the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spain's geographical position, along with its climate and topography, make it unusually vulnerable as global temperatures increase.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Germanwatch, an independent environmental organisation, ranked Spain the world's 20th most affected country in its climate risk index for 2024, just behind Nigeria and Mali.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are those who see an upside for the economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "Climate change affects how we produce, how we invest and how we consume," says Julián Cubero, head of economics of climate change at economic think tank BBVA Research.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He points to how heat can act as a drag on economic activity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We all work worse when it's hot," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he adds, a greener economy can create new jobs with greater productivity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The key is to realise that if we don't act, growth will slow down, and if it's handled right it can become an opportunity," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The long nose of the X-59 is designed to dampen the plane's sonic boom There's a weird and wonderful jet flying over the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It has the nose of anteater, parts cannibalised from other planes and a cockpit so far back the pilot depends on a camera to see where he's going.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This contraption, the X-59, might just be the future of air travel.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-59's owes its eccentric design to the problem of sonic booms.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The shockwave created by a jet breaking the sound barrier restricted Concorde to flights over the sea and barred it from lucrative routes across the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Now Nasa is working around that problem using the X-59's elongated snout to flatten supersonic booms into tolerable bumps in the background.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: On top of its bizarre appearance the X-59 boasts a remarkable lineage.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It's the latest in a series of experimental Nasa aircraft dating back to 1947 and the first plane to break the sound barrier, the Bell X-1.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Peter Coen, a 43-year Nasa veteran who manages the programme, explains the thinking behind 80 years of X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In the case of the X-1, flown through the sound barrier in 1947 by the legendary test pilot Chuck Yeager, Nasa knew a .50 calibre bullet travelled faster than the speed of sound.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: So the stumpy little aircraft was shaped like a bullet with wings added.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A mere 20 years later the X-15 rocket plane, a cylinder with tiny wings dropped from a B-52 bomber, flew to 6.7 times the speed of sound (4,520 mph) and the edge of space, paving the way for heat-resistant materials vital to the Space Shuttle.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In 1947 the Bell X-1 was the first plane to break the sound barrier Nasa is flying the X-59 in conjunction with community surveys to assess what people think when a supersonic boom is bent by the planes stretched nose and hushed up.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "We want to figure out what level of boom is acceptable to people on a regular basis," says Coen, who reckons his machine will sound "like a car door being closed across the street" when it flies past Mach 1, around 660mph at airline cruising altitude.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: With its cockpit and ejector seat taken from a T-38 training jet, its landing gear from an F-16 fighter and engine courtesy of the F-18 this jigsaw of an aircraft was assembled by Lockheed Martin for Nasa.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A camera feeding a screen in front of the pilot relies on instantaneous computer processing to get round the lack of forward vision.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It first flew in 2025 and is now breaking the sound barrier over chosen US towns.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But is there still a place for X-plane projects in a world where relatively cheap drones are being rapidly developed - not least in Ukraine's war against Russia .
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Even Nasa considered an uncrewed X-59.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But drones are not always a cheaper option.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Removing the pilot would have added the cost and complication of certifying a robot jet to fly fast over urban areas.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Plus the X-59 had to be big enough to resemble an airliner punching through the sound barrier, which in turn allowed space for a cockpit.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Nasa is no stranger to drone X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-48, a scaled down model of an airliner that blends wing and fuselage to create a single lifting body, flew in 2007.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Small was beautiful for the tiny X-48 with its 20ft wingspan as this kept the programme within budget.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "It's likely that future X-planes will be uncrewed," says Coen, before adding the vital caveats "unless the technology we're researching relates to piloting or if crewing it is more cost-effective".
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-48 was a scaled-down plane to test a blended wing and fuselage Guy Gratton, professor of Aircraft Test and Evaluation at Cranfield University, gets frustrated at the suggestion crewed test planes have had their day.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "There's a belief in certain quarters that drones can do everything.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In Ukraine they've done amazing things with drones, but if you want to carry people you can't take short-cuts." Gratton has tested light aircraft and stresses the importance of a human in the loop.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "You lose a huge amount without pilots, you miss lessons a pilot would identify, plus it can take four times as many people on the ground to test a drone." Staff monitoring signals from a drone are an indirect cost that keeps some piloted X-planes relatively affordable.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The Experimental Aircraft Programme tested systems for the Typhoon fighter.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The UK has flown its own technology testbeds and Chris Yeo was in the pilot's seat of one.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The Experimental Aircraft Programme (EAP) flew from Lancashire in 1986 and tried out core systems for the Typhoon fighter.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Yeo acknowledges the EAP's shared heritage with X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "They all research some facet of flight, and demonstrate the design is working correctly.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A lot of people say they can do something, but you only know it works when the design has been tested and certified." Forty years on from Yeo's EAP flights a new UK technology demonstrator is taking shape.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It is, says Tony Godbold who runs the project for BAE Systems, "the X-plane of our generation".
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This BAE Systems initiative pulls together 100 UK suppliers including Rolls-Royce to test out ideas that might make it into the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), a fighter due to fly in the 2030s.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The technology demonstrator will borrow engines from the existing Typhoon and fly sometime in 2028.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This has triggered great excitement in the UK's small community of qualified fast jet test pilots.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Almost every one, around 14 of them says Godbold, has already tried out this plane on a flight simulator.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: For many in the aerospace industry, the human element still matters as much as it did in Yeager's day.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "You can model a lot on computers and simulators, but the experience of test pilots is when stuff gets real, we only really learn things when we get their feedback," Godbold admits.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: There's a political dimension to such jets too.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Godbold says his plane underlines the UK's commitment to GCAP, a joint effort with Italy and Japan.

sentences.article_title: Would you buy branded clothing from your favourite tech firm?

sentences.text: She explains that it's a representation of a team and ethos "that I am impressed by and root for", and she proudly wears the jumper in videos she posts on social media. , external Nvidia certainly plays in the top league of global tech firms.
sentences.article_title: Would you buy branded clothing from your favourite tech firm?

sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Silicon is a highly effective and cheap material to use in anodes, but pure silicon expands and contracts as the battery operates and is recharged, which causes it to crack.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Given that a robot recently beat Usain Bolt's 100m sprint record, it's not the most startling achievement.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But the speed by which Freddo has been trained to walk, recognise the bottle and grasp it is impressive.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It took just a few minutes to develop those skills and upload them to Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: I'm at Vsim, a British start-up based in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey hope one day their software will control robots that can navigate and do useful tasks in the home and workplace.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It's a weird situation with robotics because actually the stuff that we find as humans to be incredibly difficult, like gymnastics, you can get robots to do reasonably well.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The stuff that humans are really good at, like fine dexterity, is really hard in robots," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Vsim founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey Freddo's skills were honed in a virtual environment, where a task can be performed  in a computer simulation millions of times.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Such virtual simulations are a common way to train robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Tech giant Nvidia has a system called Isaac Sim which works that way - Lu and Storey both worked on an early version of it.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: In 2022 they decided to set up Vsim, to build the their own training system environment and other tools.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "The underlying algorithms that we were using for most of these robotic simulations they hark back to the 1970s and 1980s, but those algorithms are not really brilliant fits for GPUs," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Angela Rayner took aim at the 'injustice' of leasehold in her conference speech Leaseholders will be given extra protections from "cowboy" property agents and hidden fees, Angela Rayner has announced.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The housing secretary told Labour's annual conference the government would legislate for a new independent regulator and launch a consultation to cap "rip off" administrative fees.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The changes would cover the estimated five million leaseholders in England and Wales who can be forced to pay a landlord for simple changes to their home, despite having bought it.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner told party activists she had heard of leaseholders being charged £250 for permission to own a pet and £400 to change their front door.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She said people in these situations were "powerless against the vested interests that only take, while giving nothing back in return".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government is already legislating , external to ban new leasehold flats, described in Labour's 2024 election manifesto as a "feudal" system where people own the right to occupy a property via a lease for a limited number of years from a freeholder, or landlord, who owns the land.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Through the Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill , ministers want a commonhold system where residents collectively own and manage their buildings.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Now, Rayner is taking aim at the web of management companies that operate between leaseholders and their effective landlords.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: She said the sector had many decent businesses which were "undermined by far too many cowboys, crooks and con artists".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: People excited at buying their own homes are "tricked" into using in-house services, meaning that "with no transparency or accountability, vultures can take advantage", Rayner added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: "We will legislate for an independent regulation to rein these cowboys in," she said, announcing legislation for an independent watchdog of property agents.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: This includes estate agents, managing agents and estate managers.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: This regulator would be able to set codes of practice, such as standards of conduct and proper complaint handling for those they regulate, and property agents will be required to obtain a licence.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: If they fall foul of the required standards, the regulator would have the power to take their licenses away, the government added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government said it wanted to bring forward the changes "as soon as possible".
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner also said new legislation would create the power for caps on permission and administration fees leaseholders pay to landlords.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: These caps would cover freehold estates and privately managed estates where people can face additional fees for making cosmetic changes to their properties and requesting documents like building safety certificates.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: A public consultation will be launched to help decide the rate of caps.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: It comes in addition to an already-announced £250 cap on yearly ground rents paid by leaseholders in England and Wales, which had stalled during the change of prime minister over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The government has said it expects the limit on ground rents - an annual fee paid by leaseholders to their freeholder - to come into force in late 2028, but MPs have called for this to be brought forward to late 2027.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner said she was "capping and then scrapping" ground rents, indicating she may try to go further than a cap.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: Rayner also said she plans to strengthen council powers to take over empty homes to meet the need for council houses and tackle homelessness.
sentences.article_title: Rayner announces crackdown on 'cowboy' leasehold property agents

sentences.text: The national inquiry involves a series of targeted, local investigations into child sexual abuse by grooming gangs A national inquiry into child sexual abuse by grooming gangs has announced that targeted investigations will take place in Birmingham and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: The inquiry said the probes would "examine the sexual abuse and exploitation of children by grooming gangs and the response of organisations responsible for protecting children" in both areas.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: Oldham in Greater Manchester, Bradford and Keighley in West Yorkshire and London were announced as the first locations for investigations earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: It is unclear whether further locations will be selected.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: Some survivors have expressed frustration that their area has not yet been included and said they were concerned about expanding the inquiry's scope.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: Fiona Goddard, who was sexually abused as a child by groups of men in Bradford, said there was clearly evidence from Birmingham and Wales "that needs to be properly heard" and welcomed their inclusion.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: But she told the BBC that the scale of the inquiry "must not come at the expense of the depth of investigation".
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: This was especially concerning, Goddard added, given "we are already almost a year into the inquiry with relatively little progress".
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: Carly, not her real name, was 12 years old when she was first groomed in Huddersfield in 2004.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: She said she could not understand "how an investigation covering an area as enormous and complex as Wales can be described as a deep dive".
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: "It's about institutions that failed children and the questions that have remained unanswered.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: It previously faced turbulence prior to launching, when abuse survivors called on former safeguarding minister Jess Phillips to quit amid claims that the government was seeking to widen the scope of the inquiry to other forms of child abuse.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: Chaired by former children's commissioner Baroness Anne Longfield, it has the power to compel individuals and institutions to explain what they "did or did not do to protect children from being sexually abused".
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: Alongside national accountability hearings, local investigations will examine what happened in specific areas, including how grooming gangs operated and what institutions knew.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: The inquiry has previously said that areas are chosen for investigation based on criteria including how victims and survivors were treated when they came forward, and whether opportunities to prevent harm were missed.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: A National Listening Project, inviting victims and survivors to share their experiences, has also been expanded, with people able to contribute through written or recorded submissions from next month.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: But Amy Clowrey, a director at Switalskis solicitors, which represents more than 50 survivors who are participating in the national inquiry, warned that clarity was needed over how evidence "from places without a local investigation" would be examined by the inquiry.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: Panel member Zoë Billingham said: "We will look carefully at what organisations knew, how decisions were made, how agencies worked together, and why opportunities to protect children were missed".
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: The Birmingham investigation may extend to surrounding or connected areas if the evidence supports it.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: Phillips, Labour MP for Birmingham Yardley, welcomed the move.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: She praised Baroness Longfield as an "amazing and robust" public servant, adding that those already taking part in the inquiry "felt that they've been heard".
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: But she said her main hope for the inquiry was for it to create "the impetus for change", adding that she did not want the process "to go on for decades".
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: Birmingham Local Conservatives, which had previously called for the city's grooming cases to be fully investigated, also welcomed the announcement - saying questions had gone unanswered for too long.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: The investigation in Wales will also examine the operation of devolved arrangements and cross-border working between organisations in Wales and England.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: The Welsh government welcomed the announcement, and said minister Delyth Jewell had met Baroness Longfield earlier this week to press for "dedicated activity" in Wales as part of the national inquiry.

sentences.text: The Welsh Conservatives and Reform also supported the news.
sentences.article_title: Grooming gangs inquiry expanded to Birmingham and Wales

sentences.text: A new NHS-style social care system for England could take decades to be implemented, economist Sir Andrew Dilnot has told the BBC.

sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme the cost of such a scheme would be "very substantial".
sentences.article_title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says

sentences.text: And with Burnham promising to put his plans before voters at the next general election, Sir Andrew said change "is now further away".

sentences.text: His pitch could, very broadly, be divided into the short term - what he hopes to achieve before a general election; and the long term - the prospectus he is beginning to assemble to put to the country when polling day comes around inside the next three years.

sentences.text: The biggest ideas have the longest timeframe and, perhaps, the greatest need for a lengthy debate in their gestation.

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: But from April 2030, if Labour win the next election, the annual earnings link will be dropped.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Knowing they would face blunt criticism about binning the existing triple lock – note the reaction of the Unite union and Labour's political rivals – it would appear the prime minister was keen to offer as much of what he hopes will be reassuring detail to many.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: Also going into the next Labour manifesto, he said, a change in the Westminster voting system and – after a review to come – the idea of a closer relationship with the European Union.

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham delivers deeply political speech with a personal core

sentences.text: In his Labour conference speech, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would "adjust" the triple lock on the state pension to help pay for a new "national care service" in England from 2030.

sentences.text: Since it was introduced by the coalition government in 2011, the triple lock has guaranteed that the UK state pension rises each year in line with whichever is the highest of inflation, average wages, or 2.5%.

sentences.text: Burnham said that from April 2030, instead, it would only rise in line with the highest of inflation or 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: The prime minister added that "it will hold its value relative to earnings over time".
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: That is important because in some years the triple lock has meant the state pension has risen faster than earnings.
sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?

sentences.text: "The removal of this permanent ratchet is to be welcomed and marks a substantial step towards a more sustainable and predictable state pension system," the IFS says.

sentences.text: It estimates that the present triple lock will increase annual state pension expenditure by £16bn a year by 2026–27, compared with if it had risen in line with average earnings growth since 2011.

sentences.article_title: Could changing the pension triple lock pay for Burnham's big social care plan?
