sentences.text: Dr Chris McCarthy says the pillow that's best for you depends on the way you sleep (branding has been obscured) "I am one of those people," says Dr Chris McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "I do take my pillow with me." You may have seen those people at the airport - a pillow stuffed under an arm as they drag their suitcases to check-in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Or you might be one yourself - attached to a pillow that's soft enough to settle into but robust enough that it's not bunched into a ball by morning.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy insists he's not being fussy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He's a top physiotherapist and knows the wrong pillow can be a pain in the neck.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He doesn't take his abroad, but as soon as he gets to his hotel he starts "faffing about" with the pillows - and he's got a tried and tested trick to make even the most lacklustre one fit for sleep.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Here's his guide to choosing the perfect pillow for you.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: What makes the perfect pillow?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: One advertised for your sleeping position?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Sliced Bread separates science fact from the marketing fiction.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy, an associate professor at the Manchester School of Physiotherapy, says the right pillow will depend on what position you sleep in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He tells the BBC's Sliced Bread podcast that most people fall into one of three categories of sleeper: side, back or front.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy discourages front sleeping as your neck is turned one way for a long period of time.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Inevitably a muscle or ligament gets stretched and a bit irritated," he says.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If there's one thing there's a really good consensus on... in the physiotherapy world about treating spinal pain, it's don't sleep on your front." When choosing a pillow, back sleepers should consider the flexion at the top of their spine, a curving that increases naturally in many people as they age.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If you have a bigger bend "it means you need a slightly thicker pillow than someone who's got a very flat back," says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For side sleepers the key measurement is the width of your shoulders.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: In general, the broader you are the thicker the pillow you will need.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But you also need to consider your mattress.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy says how much you sink into your mattress "makes a huge difference in the subsequent height you then need from the pillow".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Broad shoulders need a thick pillow [if] you're on a very firm mattress," he explains.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If you're on a softer mattress, then you need a thinner pillow because your shoulder sinks into the mattress [more]." This is less of an issue for back sleepers as they don't sink into the mattress as much as side sleepers do.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If your pillow feels too flat, McCarthy suggests placing a folded towel underneath and changing the number of folds to adjust the height.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Then you can make a rough measurement to help you pick a new one.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Specialist pillows are often advertised as contoured, ergonomic or orthopaedic - but McCarthy says their effectiveness isn't completely proven.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "There is a little bit of fairly scrappy evidence to suggest that having a little bit of a higher front of the pillow, which goes into the neck area... does help [side sleepers]." To see if a higher front helps you sleep better, you can try McCarthy's towel trick by rolling it and placing it underneath your pillow.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He urges side sleepers to pick a position that keeps their back straight.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For back sleepers, some manufacturers advertise a pillow with a dip in the middle that is raised at the sides.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: It does put people into a good sleeping position, says McCarthy, but some of his patients have found them "a bit claustrophobic".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Someone who has a large and heavy head also needs a thicker and firmer pillow, he adds.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Feather and down can keep you cool on warm nights because they wick away heat from your head, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But they can change shape during the night, particularly if the sleeper moves around a lot and the pillow can end up bunched towards the headboard.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "What starts off as a nice, flat, supported surface becomes a wedge and so your neck is then kinked up." Hollow fibre and microfibre fillings can hold shape better though they generally don't wick away heat as well, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Some are made with a firmer material in the lower half of the pillow, which help retain the shape during the night.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Schools are "crying out" for guidance from government on how pupils and teachers can use AI safely and effectively, a new report has warned.

sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Experts called it a "special surprise" to find the "incredibly sparse moth" in the habitat.

sentences.text: The fen, which is an area of low, flat, wet land, is monitored by Natur am Byth's Llŷn and Ynys Môn project, which aims to protect some of north Wales' most at risk species.
sentences.article_title: The rare Bog Grass Moth found in nature reserve for first time

sentences.text: As experts from the conservation project gathered at Cors Geirch they set up moth traps and in one night 446 moths made up of 91 different species were collected, with 19 of these being Bog Grass Moths - the first time they had been recorded in this area.

sentences.text: Natural Resources Wales said the habitat allowed wet sedges to grow - which is the only food source for the Bog Grass Moth's larvae.

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: One of the best-known meteor showers of the year is returning to our skies this week, as the Earth passes through debris left behind by Halley's Comet.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: The Orionid meteor shower is active from 2 October until 7 November and will peak overnight from 21 to 22 October.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: The display occurs at around the same time each year as the Earth passes through a trail of dust and debris left behind by Halley's Comet.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: The best time to spot the meteors will be between midnight and dawn, when the sky is at its darkest.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: As tiny particles from the comet enter the Earth's atmosphere at high speed, they heat up and produce streaks of light across the night sky that we see as meteors.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: The Orionids are particularly fast, entering the atmosphere at around 41 miles per second and can leave glowing trails which remain visible for several seconds.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: Halley's Comet is one of the most famous comets in our Solar System and has been observed from Earth for centuries.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: It takes around 76 years to complete one orbit of the Sun and was last seen from Earth in 1986.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: But while the comet itself is a rare visitor, the Earth encounters material left behind by it twice a year, resulting in the Eta Aquariid meteor shower in May and the Orionids in October.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: Halley's Comet is not expected to be visible from Earth again until 2061, but its debris will continue to produce meteor showers each year Under ideal conditions, around 10 to 20 meteors can be seen each hour at the shower's peak.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: The meteors appear to radiate from the constellation of Orion, which is where the shower gets its name, but they can appear anywhere across the night sky.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: For the best chance of seeing them, find a dark location away from street lights and with as wide a view of the sky as possible.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: Allow around 15 to 20 minutes for your eyes to adjust.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: You won't need binoculars or a telescope; the shower is best viewed with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: Viewing prospects will be rather mixed with the best conditions likely to be across southern and eastern parts of England - where there should be long clear spells, albeit with a few areas of cloud drifting across the sky from time-to-time.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: In Wales, the Midlands and Northern England it may be more of a struggle to see the meteor shower, with a slow-moving weather front providing cloud and outbreaks of rain.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: The rain is likely to turn patchier later in the night with a few cloud breaks likely to develop.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: For Scotland and Northern Ireland it will be a story of clear periods, patchy cloud and a few showers - and if the gaps between the showers are long enough you should get a view for at least some of the time.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: The Moon could also affect how many meteors are visible at the peak of the Orionids later in October, as it will be in its waxing gibbous phase, meaning its light could make some of the fainter meteors more difficult to see.
sentences.article_title: Orionid meteor shower to streak across night sky this week

sentences.text: Brighter meteors however should still be visible, particularly from darker locations away from artificial light.

sentences.text: Many farmers rely on government payments to manage their land in more environmentally-friendly ways Thousands of farmers missed out on vital government funding after online applications for a £233m green scheme for the whole of England closed down in under six hours.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Farming and environmental groups condemned the race to secure the sustainable farming incentive (SFI) funding, with some comparing it to a "frantic" online scramble to secure Glastonbury or Oasis gig tickets.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The post-Brexit scheme, which replaced EU subsidies with payments for farmers to look after nature and provide "public goods", opened at 10:00 BST on Tuesday but had run out of budget by 15:48 BST.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The government said farmers had responded "in force" to the scheme and there would be further funding opportunities for 2027.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The SFI scheme had been shut without warning last year so demand from farmers was expected to be high The National Farmers' Union (NFU) is calling for the government to explain why the scheme opened and closed so quickly, with so many farmers left out of pocket.

sentences.text: It said it wanted "clarity and urgency" from the government and added that it had made "repeated warnings of a lack of sufficient budget".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: NFU vice-president Robyn Munt said: "The rapid uptake of the scheme comes as no surprise.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "The current cashflow pressures facing farmers and growers only exacerbates that demand as they look for certainty and clarity for the year ahead." sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: When the scheme was suddenly closed without notice last year, there were concerns that some farmers might turn their backs on environmental work if they could not access the payments and demand for Tuesday's scheme was expected to be high.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The Nature Friendly Farming Network (NFFN), which helps farmers to manage land in environmentally-friendly ways, criticised the "frantic scramble" and said farmers had "faced a desperate race against time" to secure their funding agreements.

sentences.text: "We need to find a better way based on continuous, whole-farm agreements, not doors that slam shut on day one because the money has already gone." sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Apple has been ordered to pay $5.7bn (£4.3bn) in damages after a US jury found it had used another firm's tech without permission.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: Audio firm Taction Technology claimed in 2021 that Apple had infringed two of its patents for haptics systems, which enable vibrations for actions such as receiving a message or pressing a button.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: This tech is built into devices like the iPhone and Apple Watch.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: Apple said it had not used Taction's vibration tech and would appeal the verdict.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: "While we thank the jury for their consideration, we strongly disagree with today's verdict and the damages awarded, which are entirely unsupported by the facts," it said.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: "Apple's Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology, which Taction's own testing of Apple's products confirmed during trial." Haptics allow people to interact with devices by simulating the sense of touch or feel through vibrations.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: They have become a hallmark of modern devices, with smartphones, watches and video game controllers among those containing small motors that move in response to specific electronic signals.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: Apple's "Taptic Engine" system - enabling haptic feedback in its devices - first debuted with the Apple Watch in 2014.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: Since then, it has improved its underlying system, and with that expanded haptics in its devices.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: Taction, which makes headphones and gaming headsets, claimed in 2021 that these improvements infringed patents it was issued in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: It wrote in its complaint , external that by producing better haptic vibrations in its devices, Apple had been able to improve its overall user experience.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: As such, the tech giant had been "capitalising on Taction's innovation and success by selling devices that infringe [its] patents", Taction said.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: It also accused Apple of using its inventions "without license or authority".
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: A San Diego judge ruled in 2023 that Apple did not infringe upon Taction's patents.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: However, an appeal was subsequently taken up by a federal appeal circuit - resulting in a September jury trial at the US District Court for the Southern District of California which found in its favour.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: In Friday's verdict , external , jurors did not find that Apple had infringed the patents in question willingly.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: It marks one of many similar lawsuits the tech giant has defended itself against in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit

sentences.text: Model Naomi Campbell has won her appeal against a ban on being a charity trustee, after a tribunal ruled that she was unaware of misconduct at her charity Fashion for Relief.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: Campbell was banned from being a charity trustee for five years in 2024 after a watchdog found that Fashion for Relief funds had been spent on luxury hotels and spa treatments.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: However, a tribunal said on Thursday , external that the most serious instances of misconduct in the charity "were concealed" from Campbell by a fellow trustee.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: "Ms Campbell was not involved in, and did not know of, that conduct," the three-person tribunal panel said.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: The supermodel set up Fashion for Relief to help victims of Hurricane Katrina in 2005, and went on to front further campaigns for disasters and causes around the world.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: However, the charity was shut in 2023 and Campbell and two other trustees were banned the following year after a Charity Commission inquiry found "serious mismanagement and/or misconduct" at Fashion for Relief, which was not passing on as much of the money raised as it was supposed to.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: Campbell appealed, saying one of her fellow trustees, lawyer Bianka Hellmich, forged her signature and impersonated her using a fake email address to misdirect money that was intended for the charity.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: Her "only mistake" was trusting Hellmich, Campbell told the tribunal in June.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: Hellmich has denied the allegations.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: The Charity Commission opposed Campbell's challenge and said the five-year ban should be upheld.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: In its ruling, the First-Tier Tribunal panel said Campbell's claim that she was deceived had been corroborated by documentary evidence.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: "For the avoidance of doubt, we accept that both Ms Campbell's evidence, as well as her conduct during the operation of the Charity, was entirely honest," they said.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: They said Campbell did not know €4,386 (£3,750) of hotel charges from a trip to the south of France in 2018 - including €1,298 (£1,100) for dinner room service, €1,163 (£990) for spa treatments and €112 (£95) for cigarettes - had come out of the charity's expenses.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: "The panel is satisfied that Ms Campbell was not responsible for the inappropriate use of the charity's resources or any unjustified expenditure, nor did she contribute or facilitate it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Naomi Campbell wins appeal over charity ban

sentences.text: After taking a year off in 2026, thousands of festival-goers are preparing to secure a place at next year's five-day event.

sentences.text: Coach and ticket packages are due to go on sale at 18:00 BST on Thursday and general admission tickets a few days later at 09:00 on Sunday.

sentences.text: The festival has introduced an automatic queuing system on the day of the sale.

sentences.text: It may also ban you from re-entering the site.

sentences.article_title: Mistakes to avoid when buying Glastonbury tickets

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Tatjana Smith was the only South African to win a gold medal at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris Having ended a two-year exile from competitive swimming, South Africa's most successful Olympian Tatjana Smith has revealed she "lost the love" for her sport before stepping away from the pool in 2024.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The 29-year-old's decision to retire straight after the Paris Games came as a surprise, given she had just won 200m breaststroke gold in the French capital to add to her 100m title from Tokyo 2020.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: But after two years away, which included several months in which she did not swim at all, Smith says she is now "free from the things that made me hate swimming".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "My whole life, I was kind of a robot towards swimming," she told Newsday on the BBC World Service.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "You're so zoned in, you're obsessed with something, so there isn't actually time for you to think about things outside of the pool that you potentially have a passion for.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think probably everyone would think that the timing [of retirement] was the worst.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Smith on retirement and becoming South Africa’s most decorated Olympian But despite making history for her country, Smith says financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, also contributed to her decision to retire.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The financial burden on any athlete is so tough," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I relied on my parents funding me until I broke the world record at the Olympics.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: And then, all of a sudden, now people are interested in maybe sponsoring you.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "But the majority of sponsorships for athletes are based on performance.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: So then you have that pressure and expectation to always have to perform, otherwise you're not going to get paid.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think the financial side, and also being in a system where they're not really putting the athletes first, made it really difficult." Smith won her first Olympic title under her maiden name Schoenmaker, before changing her surname when she married sports agent Joel Smith in 2023.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The marriage made her part of a wider South African sporting dynasty, given that her sister-in-law is Rachel Smith, who was married to Springboks captain Siya Kolisi before their split.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Tatjana Smith admits her own marriage changed the way she thought about her future.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Thinking about families as a woman, you have to time it perfectly, because if you're pregnant, it's not like you can still compete." While children are not yet part of her journey, Smith says working out what to do next was far from easy.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I definitely understand what athletes mean from the post-Olympic depression," said the 2023 200m breaststroke world champion, who also counts Commonwealth and African titles among her achievements.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "It was such an emptiness in my life, because my whole life revolved around swimming.
